_meta.indication: Long-term treatment of adult patients with Gaucher disease type 1 (GD1) who are CYP2D6 extensive metabolizers (EMs), intermediate metabolizers (IMs), or poor metabolizers (PMs) as detected by an FDA-cleared test

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study in treatment-naïve GD1 patients
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naïve adult GD1 patients ≥16 years old with pre-existing splenomegaly and hematological abnormalities
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: percentage change in spleen volume (in MN) from baseline to 9 months compared to placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Spleen volume percentage change: -27.8% CERDELGA vs +2.3% placebo; difference -30.0% [95% CI -36.8, -23.2], p<0.0001. Hemoglobin absolute change difference 1.2 g/dL [0.6, 1.9], p=0.0006; liver volume percentage change difference -6.6% [-11.4, -1.9], p=0.0072.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (imiglucerase) non-inferiority, multicenter study in patients switching from enzyme replacement therapy
pivotal_trials.population: Adult GD1 patients previously treated with ≥3 years of enzyme replacement therapy who met pre-specified therapeutic goals at baseline
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary composite endpoint: stability in all four domains (hemoglobin level, platelet count, liver volume, spleen volume) between baseline and 12 months
pivotal_trials.n: N=159 treated patients (randomized 2:1 CERDELGA vs imiglucerase)
pivotal_trials.result: CERDELGA met non-inferiority to imiglucerase: 84.8% of CERDELGA patients met the primary composite endpoint vs 93.6% imiglucerase; lower bound of 95% CI of the 8.8% difference was -17.6%, within the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -25%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% across Trials 1 and 2) were fatigue, headache, nausea, diarrhea, back pain, pain in extremities, and upper abdominal pain. In Trial 1, arthralgia (45% vs 10% placebo) and headache (40% vs 30%) were most frequent. Key safety concern is QTc/PR/QRS prolongation with high eliglustat exposure from drug-drug interactions.
target_moa: Eliglustat is a specific inhibitor of glucosylceramide synthase (IC50 = 10 ng/mL), acting as substrate reduction therapy to reduce accumulation of glucosylceramide (GL-1) that occurs in GD1 due to acid β-glucosidase deficiency.
companion_dx_detail: An FDA-cleared test for determining CYP2D6 genotype is required to select patients (EMs, IMs, PMs); CYP2D6 genotype testing is essential for safe and effective use.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was convened for this application.

orphan_indication.text: Eliglustat for the treatment of GD1 was granted orphan status.

citations.quote: Eliglustat for the treatment of GD1 was granted orphan status and therefore is exempt from the requirement for pediatric studies under the Pediatric Research Equity Act.

summary.text: CERDELGA (eliglustat), a new molecular entity glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor, received orphan status for GD1 and was approved first cycle based on two Phase 3 trials (ENGAGE and ENCORE) plus supporting data, with no advisory committee convened and postmarketing requirements for renal and hepatic impairment PK studies.

citations.quote: Cerdelga (eliglustat tartrate), a SRT, is a new molecular entity.
Eliglustat for the treatment of GD1 was granted orphan status and therefore is exempt from the requirement for pediatric studies under the Pediatric Research Equity Act.
The substantial evidence of efficacy and safety was based on two phase 3 trials (GZGD02507-ENGAGE, GZGD02607-ENCORE) and one phase 2 trial (GZGD00304)
No Advisory Committee meeting was convened for this application.
